title: Ask for Price button in webshop

posts.name: atheetha
posts.cooked: In erpnext webshop frontend items I want to show a button “Ask for Price”. When I click that button I want to show a popup form with the products details and have some field to enter customer details like Name, Phone, Email and Comments. How can I do this. Please help with the code?

posts.name: Asief Tejani
posts.cooked:
From ChatGPT: -

Got it You can extend ERPNext’s webshop frontend by injecting custom HTML/JS into the product template (www/item_group.html or www/item.html) or by overriding via a custom app.

Here’s a minimal working example for your case:

1. Add “Ask for Price” Button in Product Page

In www/item.html (or override using Website Theme), add:

<button class="btn btn-primary" id="ask-for-price-btn">
  Ask for Price
</button>

2. Popup Modal Form (hidden initially)

Put this after the button:

<div id="askPriceModal" class="modal fade" tabindex="-1" role="dialog">
  <div class="modal-dialog" role="document">
    <div class="modal-content p-4">
      <div class="modal-header">
        <h5 class="modal-title">Ask for Price</h5>
        <button type="button" class="close" data-dismiss="modal" aria-label="Close">×</button>
      </div>
      <div class="modal-body">
        <form id="askPriceForm">
          <input type="hidden" name="item_code" value="{{ item_code }}">

          <div class="form-group">
            <label>Product</label>
            <input type="text" class="form-control" value="{{ item_name }}" readonly>
          </div>

          <div class="form-group">
            <label>Your Name</label>
            <input type="text" name="customer_name" class="form-control" required>
          </div>

          <div class="form-group">
            <label>Phone</label>
            <input type="text" name="phone" class="form-control" required>
          </div>

          <div class="form-group">
            <label>Email</label>
            <input type="email" name="email" class="form-control" required>
          </div>

          <div class="form-group">
            <label>Comments</label>
            <textarea name="comments" class="form-control"></textarea>
          </div>

          <button type="submit" class="btn btn-success">Submit</button>
        </form>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>

3. JavaScript to Handle Button + Form Submission

Add this at the bottom of the template:

<script>
  // Show modal
  document.getElementById("ask-for-price-btn").onclick = function() {
    $("#askPriceModal").modal("show");
  };

  // Handle form submit
  document.getElementById("askPriceForm").onsubmit = function(e) {
    e.preventDefault();

    let formData = {};
    new FormData(this).forEach((value, key) => formData[key] = value);

    frappe.call({
      method: "your_app.api.ask_for_price",  // backend method (see below)
      args: formData,
      callback: function(r) {
        if (!r.exc) {
          frappe.msgprint("Your request has been submitted. We will contact you soon.");
          $("#askPriceModal").modal("hide");
          document.getElementById("askPriceForm").reset();
        }
      }
    });
  };
</script>

4. Backend Python API

Create a method in your custom app, e.g. your_app/api.py:

import frappe

@frappe.whitelist(allow_guest=True)
def ask_for_price(item_code, customer_name, phone, email, comments=None):
    # You can save it as a custom DocType, or just send an email
    doc = frappe.get_doc({
        "doctype": "Lead",   # Or create your own "Price Inquiry" DocType
        "lead_name": customer_name,
        "email_id": email,
        "mobile_no": phone,
        "note": f"Inquiry for {item_code}\nComments: {comments}"
    })
    doc.insert(ignore_permissions=True)

    # (Optional) Send notification
    frappe.sendmail(
        recipients=["sales@yourcompany.com"],
        subject=f"Price Inquiry: {item_code}",
        message=f"""
        Product: {item_code}<br>
        Name: {customer_name}<br>
        Phone: {phone}<br>
        Email: {email}<br>
        Comments: {comments}
        """
    )

    return {"status": "ok"}

5. Whitelist the Method

Make sure your_app/api.py is imported in hooks.py:

app_include_js = ["/assets/your_app/js/custom.js"]  # if needed

With this setup:

  • A button appears on each product page.
  • Clicking it opens a popup form.
  • Submission calls your backend method → saves a Lead (or custom DocType) + sends an email.

Do you want me to build this using a custom DocType called “Price Inquiry” (cleaner than stuffing it into Leads), or should I adapt it directly to Leads since ERPNext already handles them?
